stories.title: ISSB urged to make its nature-related disclosure a standard - ESG Dive
Westlake sets 2030 emissions reduction target
stories.summary: Westlake Corporation has released its ninth annual sustainability report. After achieving a 20 percent reduction in Scope 1 and 2 emissions per ton of production from a 2016 baseline, the company has committed to a further 5 percent reduction by 2030 using a 2024 baseline.

stories.title: Westlake highlights emissions and water initiatives
stories.summary: Westlake Corporation released its 2025 sustainability report, noting a 20 percent reduction in Scope 1 and 2 emissions from a 2016 baseline. The company now targets an additional 5 percent reduction by 2030. CEO Jean-Marc Gilson highlighted a global water risk assessment as part of the effort.

stories.title: Deloitte survey finds shift in corporate sustainability
stories.summary: A Deloitte survey of over 2,100 C-suite leaders suggests corporate sustainability is entering a more disciplined phase. Organisations are moving from broad ambitions to focused execution embedded across the business. The report notes a greater emphasis on return on investment and technology as an enabler for resilience.

stories.title: New grant for large businesses to defray costs of sustainability reporting - Singapore Economic Development Board (EDB)
Porada publishes first sustainability report
stories.summary: Italian furniture manufacturer Porada has published its first sustainability report for the 2025 financial year. The company is not subject to mandatory reporting requirements but chose to follow the Voluntary Sustainability Reporting Standard for SMEs. The move marks a formal step toward greater transparency for the family-owned business.

stories.title: University of Liverpool wins Green Gown Award
stories.summary: The University of Liverpool has won the Reporting with Influence category at the 2026 Green Gown Awards. The award recognises the institution's commitment to transparency and embedding sustainability into strategic decision-making. The ceremony was held in Leeds to celebrate initiatives across the higher education sector.

stories.title: Bank of Uganda governor urges sustainability reporting
stories.summary: Bank of Uganda Governor Michael Atingi-Ego has urged businesses to begin sustainability reporting immediately, citing climate-related risks to economic growth and financial stability. He told firms they should not wait for 2028, adding that while the first report need not be perfect, it must be honest.

stories.title: HUDCO releases ESG report for 2026
stories.summary: Housing and Urban Development Corporation Limited has released its ESG report for the 2025-26 financial year. Titled Financing Sustainable Cities Today, Shaping a Resilient Tomorrow, the document anchors the company's strategy in a philosophy of profitability with social justice and marks a shift from conventional financial disclosures.

stories.title: TNFD calls for mandatory nature reporting standard
stories.summary: The Taskforce on Nature-related Financial Disclosures has asked the International Sustainability Standards Board to develop a standalone mandatory standard for nature-related risks. The taskforce argues this would provide more decision-useful information for investors than the board's current proposal for a voluntary practice statement.

stories.title: EU and UK Agree to Link Carbon Markets in 2028, With £6.5 Billion of Exports Set for CBAM Relief - CEO Magazyn
EU And UK Seal Carbon Market Deal, Opening Billions In CO2 Storage Opportunities - Carbon Herald
Uttar Pradesh and IIT Roorkee launch carbon credit model
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh and IIT Roorkee have launched a carbon credit model to help farmers earn income through sustainable agricultural practices. The pilot project in Saharanpur aims to convert carbon stored in soil and trees into verified credits that can be sold in carbon markets.

stories.title: EU recognises non-EU carbon pricing schemes
stories.summary: The European Union has recognised carbon pricing schemes from 24 countries, including Albania, Montenegro, Serbia and Turkey. This decision allows CO2 taxes paid in these nations to be considered when calculating costs under the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism for exported goods.

stories.title: UK and EU to link carbon markets
stories.summary: The UK and EU have agreed to link their carbon trading markets starting in 2028. The agreement is part of a broader package intended to reduce trade friction for food and drink, with further talks scheduled to continue through next year regarding the UK re-joining the EU electricity market.

stories.title: UK and EU agree to link carbon markets
stories.summary: The UK and EU have agreed to link their carbon trading markets starting in 2028. The agreement is part of a broader package intended to reduce trade friction for food and drink, with further talks scheduled to continue through next year regarding the UK re-joining the EU electricity market.

stories.title: Spain approves ETS2 carbon market for buildings and road transport
stories.summary: Spain has approved a decree-law establishing the ETS2 carbon market for buildings and road transport. Fuel suppliers will handle compliance and reporting, with costs potentially passed to consumers. Households are exempt from direct registration or allowance surrender. The system begins operations on 1 January 2028.

stories.title: Explainer: What are the UK and EU carbon markets and what does linking them mean? - Reuters
NLC outlines how communities can benefit from carbon credits
stories.summary: The National Land Commission is calling for faster community land registration to facilitate carbon credit participation. Deputy Director Bernard Opaa noted that carbon credits are tied to land ownership and consent. The commission is currently seeking clarity on who owns, uses, and benefits from land-based carbon assets.

stories.title: Ghana becomes first African country to secure TREES forest carbon credits
stories.summary: Ghana is the first African nation to secure jurisdictional forest carbon credits under the REDD+ Environmental Excellence Standard. The issuance covers 6.5 million tonnes of emission reductions achieved between 2017 and 2021. The country expects $43 million in payments from the sale of four million credits.

stories.title: Kazakhstan's aluminium exports to the EU reach 110,184t as CBAM reshapes trade outlook - AL Circle
Korea International Trade Association opens EU regulatory response channel
stories.summary: The Korea International Trade Association has launched a Brussels-based channel to address EU industrial regulations. The initiative aims to mitigate cost burdens from policies like the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism and the Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation. The association is coordinating its response with local operating companies.

stories.title: COP31 climate summit enters overtime
stories.summary: Diplomats at COP31 in Antalya have entered overtime after failing to reach a deal by the Friday deadline. The latest draft omits references to phasing out fossil fuels, a move campaigners describe as a regression. The summit is expected to continue until a consensus is reached.

stories.title: COP31 draft deal drops fossil fuel references
stories.summary: The COP31 summit has entered overtime as negotiators debate a draft deal that excludes fossil fuel phase-out language. The proposal relies on carbon capture technology and makes electrification an optional target. References to the health co-benefits of climate mitigation were also removed from the text.

stories.title: COP31 talks run overtime as fossil fuel divisions deepen
stories.summary: COP31 negotiations have extended past the scheduled deadline following the removal of fossil fuel transition language from the draft agreement. A new global electrification target is proposed, though critics warn the lack of clean power guarantees could inadvertently encourage continued reliance on coal and gas.

stories.title: Disagreements over climate facts slow COP31 action
stories.summary: Negotiations at COP31 are facing delays due to a dispute over the timing of a key global warming assessment. Diplomats have expressed concern that the disagreement threatens the scientific foundation of climate action. The summit remains deadlocked over finance and emissions targets as the deadline passes.

stories.title: COP31 on the brink as fossil fuel fight dominates
stories.summary: Negotiators at COP31 are struggling to finalize a deal as divisions over fossil fuels and climate finance persist. The current draft includes a voluntary 35% electrification goal for 2035, which critics note could be achieved using fossil fuels. The text also acknowledges that warming will exceed 1.5°C.

stories.title: COP31 talks go into overtime
stories.summary: Climate talks in Antalya have breached their Friday deadline as nearly 200 countries remain unable to agree on a draft deal. The current text contains no mention of fossil fuels, leaving negotiators deadlocked. Brazil’s climate secretary noted that at this point, no one is happy.

stories.title: Nations row over fossil fuels as COP31 goes into overtime - AFP.com
Activists condemn slimmed-down COP31 draft
stories.summary: Negotiators at COP31 have published a slimmed-down draft that removes all references to fossil fuels. The document instead emphasizes carbon capture and storage technology. Activists are also protesting the removal of language regarding human rights and environmental defenders that had been previously included in the text.

stories.title: China and Australia endorse electrification pledge
stories.summary: China and Australia have jointly endorsed a voluntary goal to increase electricity's share of global energy consumption to 35% by 2035. While the pledge aims to keep the 1.5°C goal within reach, the joint statement makes no mention of fossil fuels, consistent with the broader summit trend.

stories.title: Fossil fuel fightback drives COP31 climate talks into overtime - Financial Times
COP31 heads into overtime
stories.summary: The COP31 climate summit has entered overtime as negotiators remain divided over the final cover decision. Key points of contention include the exclusion of language regarding a transition away from fossil fuels and the mechanisms for financing adaptation efforts in vulnerable nations.

stories.title: COP31 deal elusive as fossil fuel fight deepens - Arab News
Namibian students build robots from waste
stories.summary: Students at St. Barnabas Primary School in Windhoek are constructing robots from discarded plastic bottles and bags. The project aims to spread a green message through the creation of functional models from local waste. The school is located in Namibia, where circular economy initiatives are being highlighted.

stories.title: South African Plastics Pact releases 2030 roadmap
stories.summary: The South African Plastics Pact has published its performance data for 2025 targets alongside a new roadmap for 2030. Managed by GreenCape, the initiative coordinates retailers, brand owners, and recyclers across the plastics value chain. The pact aims to guide members toward its next set of ambitious targets.

stories.title: Mexico's AMRLU awards tyre recycling efforts
stories.summary: The Responsible Used Tyre Management Association in Mexico presented its 2026 Circular Merit Awards to recognize contributions to tyre recovery. Winners included Bridgestone, Michelin, and Pirelli, alongside various shredding and processing firms. The awards highlight efforts across the entire value chain of end-of-life tyre management.

stories.title: COP31 hosts face criticism over waste
stories.summary: As COP31 convenes in Türkiye, the event has become a significant marketing opportunity for local institutions. Observers have noted a discrepancy between official rhetoric at the summit and domestic environmental conditions. The hosts have been accused of failing to practice the sustainability measures they advocate for internationally.

stories.title: Recycle Now initiative launches in Europe
stories.summary: EUROPEN and several partners have founded Recycle Now, a cross-sector initiative seeking to unify circular economy approaches across Europe. The group has issued a manifesto to European institutions, citing fragmented national systems and insufficient investment in recycling infrastructure as primary obstacles to a functioning market for secondary raw materials.

stories.title: South African Plastics Pact Celebrates Progress Towards A Circular Economy For Plastic Packaging At Its 6th Annual Membe
stories.summary: The members of the South African Plastics Pact, a pioneering voluntary industry body, have concluded the 6th Annual Member Conference, a two-day event which included the release of the complete performance dataset tracking its original 2025 circular economy targets, alongside the launch of an action-oriented Roadmap and priority levers designed

stories.summary: How cities can lead the reuse revolution Reuseable packaging systems often fail at small-scale, which is why many of the most exciting projects in this area EUROPEN, the Circular Economy Network, Konfederacja Lewiatan, and the Croatian Business Council for Sustainable Development have founded Recycle Now, a cross-sector initiative pursuing a

stories.title: Infrastructure projects adopt circular economy methods
stories.summary: Major construction projects, including the Turin-Lyon high-speed line and the Paris Metro, are applying circular economy principles to excavation waste. The approach aims to reuse rocks, groundwater, and retired machinery. The strategy frames construction sites as locations where resources are managed rather than simply discarded as waste.

stories.summary: Increasingly the Action Agenda at the annual COP Summits is where the action is - but the fraught negotiations help drive that real world progress Frustration, and tiredness, are building in Antalya. Questions about how things are going result in shrugged shoulders, shaken heads, weary laughter. Fears are growing the

stories.title: Brazilian waste-tracking tech debuts at COP31
stories.summary: Brazil has introduced Rastreia BR, a technology designed to verify the results of global circular economy initiatives. Developed by the Brazilian Agency for Industrial Development, the tool tracks waste from origin to reinsertion as raw material. It will be integrated into the Istanbul Platform to connect global solutions.

stories.title: Audi creates subsidiary for vehicle recycling
stories.summary: Audi is launching Audi Circular Solutions GmbH in 2027 to manage vehicle dismantling and recycled material recovery. The subsidiary will focus on expanding parts reuse and reducing dependence on virgin resources. The company intends to turn the end of a vehicle's life cycle into a profitable business model.

stories.title: COP31 Players Discuss Road Ahead for Electrification
stories.summary: Zulfugar Graphics/Shutterstock Save for later Print Download Share LinkedIn Twitter Despite stark divisions across parties at COP31, the Global Electrification Pledge has gained considerable backing , with many nations already looking ahead to implementation.

stories.title: BBVA recognized for electrification funding
stories.summary: BBVA has been featured in the Electrification Delivery Package at COP31 for its financial support of energy and transportation initiatives. The bank reported channeling nearly 60 billion euros into sustainable business activities between January 2025 and September 2026. Over 260 companies are included in the global initiative.

stories.title: Global Briefing: Amazon to invest further $7bn in clean energy in India by 2030
stories.summary: Plus the race to host BBNJ secretariat heats up, Google inks 50MW geothermal PPA, and FIFA is under fire for 'record of failure' on climate

stories.title: Meta’s Sustainability Report: Net Zero, Water & Circularity
stories.summary: Across the globe, Meta has offices in more than 90 cities, operating with almost 80,000 employees. Its ambition is to build technology that helps connect people, build communities and grow businesses. Alongside building communication infrastructure, Meta focuses on scaling its work on environmental stewardship through its network of data centres.

stories.title: Meta to review 2030 climate targets
stories.summary: Meta is re-evaluating its climate timelines after reporting a 45 percent year-on-year increase in emissions for 2025. The company previously set goals to achieve net zero across its value chain by 2030. The tech giant is currently reconsidering its carbon intensity targets in light of recent performance.

stories.title: Spain pledges 100 percent renewable electricity by 2040
stories.summary: Spain has announced a strategy to reach 100 percent renewable electricity generation by 2040, with a goal of a fully decarbonized economy by 2050. The country joins several other European nations in pledging to phase out fossil fuels. The plan aligns with existing national climate and energy laws.

stories.title: COP31 meets as climate records break
stories.summary: COP31 in Antalya coincided with the warmest October on record and an early Arctic polar vortex collapse. Global CO2 emissions are projected to drop 0.4 percent this year, partly due to clean energy growth and partly due to energy supply reductions caused by conflict. The climate is cooperating.

stories.title: KKR buys minority stake in Gentari India
stories.summary: KKR has acquired a minority stake in Gentari Renewables India to fund the expansion of its 8 GW clean energy portfolio. Gentari will retain operational control of the business. The company cites rising power demand and supportive policy fundamentals as reasons for its continued focus on the region.

stories.title: Businesses push for 35 percent electrification goal
stories.summary: More than 130 international businesses and financial groups have asked COP31 delegates to commit to 35 percent electrification of final energy demand by 2035. The coalition wants a clear path for transport, buildings and industry. They are waiting for a signal from the conference.

stories.title: OPINION | Why energy productivity will define the next industrial era - The Week
COP31 unveils electrification finance package
stories.summary: UN Climate Change and partners launched the AMPLIFi financing mechanism at COP31 to scale clean power and grid modernization. Backed by over 150 countries, the initiative aims to mobilize 5 billion pounds in private and institutional capital. The United Kingdom provided an initial 400 million pounds.

stories.title: Meta reconsiders 2030 net zero goal
stories.summary: Meta is re-evaluating its 2030 net zero emissions target as energy demands from AI data centers increase. The company cited the AI boom as a reason for adjusting its timelines and interim milestones. Climate pledges are currently being subjected to the requirements of compute.

research.title: Approximate Adjoint Models for Memory and Compute-Efficient Online Learning of Hybrid Models
research.summary: Announce Type: cross Abstract: Differentiable programming enables online calibration of numerical models by minimizing errors accumulated along simulated trajectories. This includes estimating physical parameters and training neural sub-models in hybrid configurations. Gradients are typically computed using adjoint methods, or backpropagation. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Evaluation of machine-learning and deep-learning SPEI drought forecasts against persistence across timescales and lead times in Bangladesh
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Bangladesh, home to nearly 178 million people, is highly vulnerable to recurring droughts that threaten food security and rural livelihoods. Machine-learning and deep-learning models are increasingly used to forecast drought indices such as the Standardized Precipitation. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Extremes on Rewind: Generating 1,000-Member Ensembles Initialized at a Final Condition
research.summary: Announce Type: replace Abstract: Scenario planning for rare, high-impact events often requires massive ensembles to stochastically sample relevant trajectories. Although autoregressive weather emulators can efficiently generate such ensembles, isolating trajectories of interest requires sifting through petabytes of data, a challenge. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: From FAIR to AWARE: Data Readiness for Agentic AI in the Earth Sciences
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial intelligence in the Earth sciences is beginning to act: prototype agents already search archives, run simulations and draft analyses. Scientific data were curated for researchers who bring expert judgement, an autonomous agent cannot be assumed. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Multi-scale dynamics of deep convective self-aggregation. Part I: physical-space structures and energy variance budget
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Vertically resolved budget analyses of frozen moist static energy (FMSE) variance within a cloud-resolving model provide a rigorous perspective on the equilibrium state of deep convective self-aggregation. The analysis reveals that the variance budget is governed. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Multi-scale dynamics of deep convective self-aggregation. Part II: scale-by-scale budget and mesoscale self-similarity
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: This work investigates deep convective self-aggregation in the space of scales, extending the physical-space analysis of Part I. We introduce a novel theoretical framework by examining and deriving a generalized Yaglom equation for the second-order structure. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Solving the puzzle of tropical cyclone track bifurcation
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Tropical cyclones whose predicted tracks bifurcate are among the most dreaded storms in disaster planning. Understanding when and why these bifurcations occur has been a long-standing puzzle in track forecasting. We address this issue by introducing. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Xaurora: Generative Weather Forecasting with Denoising Stochastic Interpolants from a Foundation Model Prior
research.summary: Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Deep learning has revolutionised weather forecasting in recent years, especially through atmospheric foundation models, which offer competitive skill for a fraction of the computational costs of classic physics-based models. However, most existing foundation models are deterministic. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
